chunks: A group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Ibn Sinan, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Sleep does not break the ablution in any part of the prayer.
ai.seo_question: Does sleeping during prayer break ablution (wudu)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that sleeping during any part of the prayer does not break ablution (wudu), a ruling derived from the principle that sleep only nullifies wudu if accompanied by loss of consciousness or bodily emissions. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction is crucial for maintaining the continuity of prayer (salat) without requiring the worshipper to perform wudu again, provided they remain within the prayer's framework. The narration underscores the precision of Imami legal reasoning in distinguishing between mere sleep and deep unconsciousness.
